title: The 1970s Green Flash Phenomenon: Why Does the Sun Turn Emerald?

scenes.text: A fleeting green flash appears at sunset over the Pacific
Most commonly observed over the clear horizons of the Pacific Ocean
The flash lasts less than 2 seconds and is caused by atmospheric refraction
1950s scientific illustration of the green flash effect

scenes.label: REAL PHENOMENON
scenes.sub: Explained by physics, yet still awe‑inspiring

scenes.text: Follow if you can't stop asking why.

description: The green flash is a genuine optical event that turns the setting sun emerald for a heartbeat. Learn the science behind this brief marvel. Follow for more sky mysteries.
